payload.summary: Accept the breakdown-reuse refactor and the habitat-invariant clarification. Reject the proposed root-demand comment because it adds an unsupported calibration claim rather than a neutral explanation of the current simplification.

votes.rationale: `engine.rs` computes `substrate_oxygenation_breakdown()` for stage metrics and then `step_substrate_zones()` immediately recomputes it against the same state. That repeats the same oxygenation math and habitat-registry work for no behavioral benefit. Refactoring `step_substrate_zones` to consume or return a precomputed breakdown improves efficiency and also guarantees the traced values are exactly the ones applied to the layers.

The current comment already explains the model split: rooted oxygenation is handled as a separate ROL bonus instead of inside the base diffusive demand term. The proposed addition goes beyond clarification and asserts that the default `rol_rate_cm_per_g` is a literature-calibrated net parameter that already absorbs root respiration. That claim is not established by the code or nearby documentation, so adding it would risk misleading future maintainers.

`substrate_root_activity_factor()` depends on an implicit habitat-registry invariant: `SubstrateSurface` currently includes the footprint top surface as well as interstitial matrix area, so subtracting the footprint isolates the root-colonizable interstitial portion. A short inline comment documenting that physical meaning is worthwhile because it makes the dependency explicit and reduces the risk of a future habitat-formula change silently breaking the calculation.
